name: ELO_145AB_PushButton_CircuitIX_LED_3Wire
description: Push button switch 145...AB, M30 contactless reed pushbutton, Circuit IX (N.O. contact + red LED illumination, Namur), AMP Superseal connector.
notes: Pinout/circuit is Circuit IX from the ordering key ('145 1 0 5 A B' = Circuit IX, LED colour red, Namur, AMP Superseal connector). The LED pin (P3) is modeled with device-side role INPUT, not OUTPUT: current flows FROM the ECU INTO the device to drive the LED, so from the device's own perspective it is receiving a signal even though the overall part is a SENSOR device_type — this is an intentional exception to the simple device_type-implies-default-role pattern. The 160 ohm/1.6W resistor (parallel across the switch contact) and 510 ohm/0.5W resistor (in series with the LED) are both current-limiting/protective in function per the datasheet's explicit power ratings, not diagnostic sense resistors, so neither pin carries a diagnostics_required flag. Max. switching/LED currents are not explicitly stated in the datasheet; derived from V/R below — verify against the exact ordering-key suffix before production use.

connectors.name: X1
connectors.mounting: M30x1 threaded body, SW36 nut, AMP-Super-Seal 3-pole shell

signals.name: ELO_145AB_RET
signals.description: Common return shared by the switch contact and the LED branch (connector pin 1).

signals.name: ELO_145AB_SW
signals.description: N.O. reed contact closes momentarily while button is pressed; 160 ohm/1.6W resistor wired in parallel across the contact (switch protection/bleed — not a diagnostic sense resistor in this design).

signals.name: ELO_145AB_LED
signals.description: Red LED illumination drive input from the ECU, via a 510 ohm/0.5W series current-limiting resistor. Modeled as device-side INPUT (device receives the drive signal) even though the part's device_type is SENSOR.
